questions.prompt: The general addresses his weary soldiers before the battle.
questions.answer: Dux fessōs mīlitēs ante proelium affātur.

questions.prompt: The prophet will speak the truth to the anxious king.
questions.answer: Vātēs vēra rēgī sollicitō fābitur.

questions.prompt: Speak, messenger, what the goddess has ordered.
questions.answer: Fāre, nūntie, quae dea imperāverit.

questions.prompt: We foretell that the war will be long.
questions.answer: Longum bellum futūrum esse praefāmur.

questions.prompt: The old man will speak with trembling voice about ancient battles.
questions.answer: Senex tremente vōce dē proeliīs antīquīs fābitur.

questions.prompt: Aeneas addresses his sorrowful companions with kindly words.
questions.answer: Aenēās maestōs sociōs verbīs benignīs affātur.

questions.prompt: Speak openly, so that all may understand your plan.
questions.answer: Fāre apertē, ut omnēs cōnsilium tuum intellegant.

questions.prompt: All true things must be spoken before the senate.
questions.answer: Omnia vēra ante senātum fanda sunt.

questions.prompt: The queen, having addressed the guest, departed into the garden.
questions.answer: Rēgīna, hospitem affāta, in hortum discessit.

questions.prompt: The poet seeks immortal fame by speaking.
questions.answer: Poēta fandō laudem immortālem quaerit.

questions.prompt: I shall be the first to speak about the impending dangers.
questions.answer: Ego prīmus dē perīculīs imminentibus fābor.

questions.prompt: The priest saw unspeakable deeds in the dark grove.
questions.answer: Sacerdōs facta nefanda in lūcō obscūrō vīdit.

questions.prompt: The commander kindly addresses the conquered enemies.
questions.answer: Imperātor victōs hostēs clēmenter affātur.

questions.prompt: The mother, having addressed her dying daughter, could not hold back her tears.
questions.answer: Māter, fīliam morientem affāta, lacrimās tenēre nōn potuit.

questions.prompt: The shepherd will speak about the flock wandering through the mountains.
questions.answer: Fābitur pāstor dē grege per montēs errante.

questions.prompt: Before the battle we foretell what fortune is to come.
questions.answer: Ante pugnam praefāmur quae fortūna ventūra sit.

questions.prompt: When the prophet had spoken, all fell silent.
questions.answer: Cum vātēs fātus esset, omnēs siluērunt.

questions.prompt: Tell me who sent you into this forest.
questions.answer: Fāre mihi, quis tē in hanc silvam mīserit.

questions.prompt: The sailors had no time for speaking about the storm.
questions.answer: Nautae dē tempestāte fandī tempus nōn habēbant.

questions.prompt: The leader, having first addressed his soldiers, gave the signal.
questions.answer: Dux mīlitēs, prius affātus, signum dedit.

questions.prompt: What the gods forbid, those things must not be spoken.
questions.answer: Quae dī prohibent, ea nōn sunt fanda.

questions.prompt: I shall speak openly about the crime which all conceal.
questions.answer: Fābor apertē dē scelere quod omnēs cēlant.
